one_line: Deficiency in the NLRP3 inflammasome or caspase-1 protects APP/PS1 mice from Alzheimer's-associated spatial memory loss and amyloid beta deposition by shifting microglia to a protective M2 phenotype.
summary: This study investigates the role of the NLRP3 inflammasome in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis. The authors demonstrate elevated active caspase-1 expression in the brains of humans with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and AD. Using the APP/PS1 mouse model of AD crossed with NLRP3- or caspase-1-deficient mice, they show that ablation of the inflammasome protects against spatial memory loss and other AD-like sequelae. Furthermore, this deficiency reduced brain levels of active caspase-1 and IL-1β while enhancing amyloid beta (Aβ) clearance. The neuroprotective effect appears to be driven by a shift in microglial cells towards an M2 anti-inflammatory and highly phagocytic phenotype, ultimately resulting in decreased Aβ plaque deposition.

key_claims.claim: NLRP3 inflammasome is activated in human MCI and AD brains.
key_claims.evidence: Demonstration of strongly enhanced active caspase-1 expression in human MCI and AD brains.

key_claims.claim: NLRP3 or caspase-1 deficiency protects against AD-associated memory loss and sequelae.
key_claims.evidence: NLRP3-/- or caspase-1-/- APP/PS1 mice were largely protected from loss of spatial memory; tested via Morris Water Maze and object recognition tests.

key_claims.claim: Inflammasome deficiency decreases Aβ deposition by skewing microglia to an M2 phenotype.
key_claims.evidence: Decreased deposition of Aβ in APP/PS1 mice, accompanied by microglial shift to M2 phenotype determined by FACS analysis and qPCR for M1/M2 markers.

methods.design: Preclinical animal study with ex vivo human brain tissue analysis
methods.population: C57/Bl6 background mice (WT, NLRP3-/-, APP/PS1, APP/PS1/NLRP3-/-, Caspase-1-/-, APP/PS1/Caspase-1-/-); Human MCI and AD brain tissue
